tasks.short: Read CVs in Recruitee and agency profiles against the vacancy and job order, decide who goes forward.

today.trigger: New applications land in Recruitee, or a site manager sends a job order for warehouse or transport staff.
steps: Open the vacancy in Recruitee and reread the requirements (licence C/CE, code 95, forklift, VCA, shift availability).
Read each CV and motivation letter, check certificates and availability.
Compare agency-supplied flex profiles with the job order in the agency portal.
Move candidates to the next stage or reject, with a short note.
drudgery: Reading near-identical, often AI-written CVs for order picker roles
Checking licence and certificate dates by hand
Retyping notes between Recruitee and agency portals
today.time_sinks: Volume roles in peak season (Q4) bring hundreds of applications per vacancy, most screened in a few minutes each but all by hand.

lenses.faster: A model extracts licences, certificates, shift availability and site distance into a fixed checklist per candidate and ranks with reasons; the recruiter reads the checklist and the CV only where it matters, cutting screening time by about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: A new application in Recruitee triggers extraction and a ranked shortlist with reasons; nothing moves stage until the recruiter decides, and no rejection is sent on the score alone.
lenses.ambitious: Screen flex workers sent by the three agencies with the same checklist as direct hires, a group nobody checks today; demand would grow because site managers would ask for it on every order.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping certificate dates; recruiters want more time phoning the borderline candidates who look weak on paper but fit the shift.
lenses.options: Showing the shortlist under two weightings (strict on certificates versus willing to train for forklift via Studytube) changes who gets invited, not just how fast.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter spends the week on borderline cases and on setting the must-have versus trainable criteria with each site manager, and gains the right to sign off the screening criteria; the job becomes more expert.
reach: Take over the HR Administrator's certificate check on new hires by learning the Studytube certificate data.
Absorb part of the agency order intake from site planners by learning the agency portal contracts.

tasks.human_edge: Judging motivation, gaps in a CV, and whether someone who lacks a certificate can be trained, and carrying the legal duty that no rejection rests only on a score.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching candidates is a selection decision under GDPR Art. 22 and later high-risk under the AI Act, so the recruiter must lead and the model only extracts and ranks with reasons.

in_practice.trigger: New application or agency profile arrives in Recruitee or the agency portal.
steps: Model extracts licences, certificates, shift availability, travel distance and language into a fixed checklist.
Rules flag hard must-haves that are missing or expired.
Model ranks candidates against the vacancy with a one-line reason each.
Recruiter reviews shortlist and borderline cases and moves stages in Recruitee.
Decision and reasons are logged per candidate.
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter decides every stage move and every rejection; the score is advice only.
data_needed: Vacancy requirements per role and site
Certificate types and validity rules (VCA, forklift, code 95)
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate notes and an audit log kept at least six months

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 builds a profile from the application and calculates a match score against open vacancies.
67% of US hiring leaders use AI for CV screening; 71% believe most applications are AI-written; 26% fear missing candidates.
No rejection may rest solely on automated scoring; review must be meaningful.
CV screening tools almost always need prior works council consent under WOR art. 27.

risks: Recruiters rubber-stamp the ranking, which makes the review meaningless under GDPR Art. 22.
Bias against older workers or non-Dutch speakers if language or gaps weigh too much.
Introducing it without OR consent makes the decision voidable.
From 2 December 2027 this is high-risk under Annex III 4(a) with oversight and logging duties.
research_questions: How often does the recruiter's decision differ from the top-ranked candidates in a three-month shadow run?
Does the AFAS Profit 8 match score work with vacancies kept in Recruitee, or only AFAS vacancies?
Will the OR consent to ranked screening if rejections remain fully manual?
What share of rejected candidates would have passed if certificates were treated as trainable?

tasks.short: Explain shifts, pay scale, CAO allowances, site conditions and growth paths to candidates by phone and mail.

today.trigger: A candidate asks a question, reaches a phone screen, or gets an invitation or offer.
steps: Look up the CAO scale, shift allowances and travel allowance for the role.
Check the shift pattern and working conditions with the site manager.
Explain by phone or write an email in Dutch or English, sometimes Polish via a colleague.
Answer follow-up questions on contract type and flex-to-fixed paths.
drudgery: Answering the same questions on night allowance and travel cost every week
Looking up the right CAO table per site
Rewriting the same email for each candidate
today.time_sinks: Repeated phone calls and emails with the same questions, often in the evening after shifts end.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the answer from the approved role fact sheet (CAO scale, shift allowances, site, schedule) and the recruiter checks and sends, saving about 45% of the time.
lenses.autonomous: A candidate question in Recruitee or a mailbox triggers a draft from the fact sheet; standard questions get a reply after recruiter approval, anything about pay outside the scale or contract terms goes to the recruiter.
lenses.ambitious: Serve candidates for night shifts and Polish-speaking flex workers for the first time with answers in their language outside office hours; demand would grow as more candidates ask before applying.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses looking up the same CAO table; recruiters want more of the real conversations about growth paths and whether night shifts fit someone's life.
lenses.options: Little here: the facts are fixed by the CAO, so multiple drafts change tone, not the decision.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter maintains one approved fact sheet per role and site with Compensation and Benefits, and decides which questions may get an approved standard answer; the job becomes somewhat more expert.
reach: Take over drafting role fact sheets from the Compensation and Benefits Specialist by learning the CAO scale tables.
Answer onboarding questions now handled by the HR Administrator by learning the AFAS onboarding steps.

tasks.human_edge: Reading hesitation on the phone, explaining what a night shift in a cold store really means, and handling pay questions where a wrong promise becomes a contractual issue.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a free-text question plus the approved fact sheet into a checkable reply inside a fixed send workflow.

in_practice.trigger: Candidate question arrives by email, Recruitee message or the careers page.
steps: Classify the question (pay, shifts, location, contract, other).
Model drafts a reply in the candidate's language from the role fact sheet only.
Recruiter approves or edits; pay outside the scale goes to the recruiter by default.
Reply is sent and stored on the candidate record.
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter approves each reply; a candidate-facing chatbot would have to say it is AI at the first turn.
data_needed: Approved fact sheet per role and site (CAO scale, allowances, shift pattern)

evidence.claim: Recruiter-reviewed emails need no AI label; a candidate-facing chatbot must disclose it is AI at the first turn, fines up to EUR 15 million or 3% of turnover.
Language models can draft accurate replies from a fixed fact sheet when retrieval is limited to approved text.

risks: A wrong statement on pay or allowances creates an expectation the CAO does not support.
Fact sheets go stale after CAO indexation.
Translated replies carry errors no recruiter can check.
research_questions: What share of candidate questions in the last quarter could be answered from a fact sheet alone?
Does a reply outside office hours raise the share of candidates who apply or accept?
Who owns updating the fact sheets after each CAO indexation?

tasks.short: Pick the best candidates after interviews and advise the site manager who to hire.

today.trigger: Interviews for a vacancy are done, or a manager asks for candidates.
steps: Collect interview feedback in Recruitee, chase missing scores.
Compare candidates on requirements, motivation and availability.
Write a short recommendation to the hiring manager.
Discuss by Teams or phone and agree on who gets an offer.
drudgery: Rewriting scattered notes into a comparison
today.time_sinks: Waiting for and chasing manager feedback, then building a comparison by hand.

lenses.faster: A model assembles the scorecards into a side-by-side comparison with gaps marked and drafts the recommendation; the recruiter writes the judgment, saving about 25%.
lenses.autonomous: When the last interview closes, missing scorecards are chased automatically and a comparison is prepared; the recommendation itself stays with the recruiter.
lenses.ambitious: Make a hiring recommendation for agency flex workers being converted to fixed contracts, a decision today made informally by shift leads; demand would grow because conversions happen every season.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses chasing scorecards; recruiters want more time on the actual discussion with the manager about fit and the 90-day outcome.
lenses.options: Showing two candidates against the 90-day retention record of past hires for that site and shift changes the choice, not only the effort.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter becomes the person who links selection choices to 90-day retention per site and challenges managers with that data; more expert.
reach: Take over conversion advice for flex workers from HR Business Partners by learning the CAO chain rule and the flex contract terms.

tasks.human_edge: Weighing interview impressions, team fit and the manager's real needs, and owning a recommendation that must be explainable to the candidate and the AP.
tasks.pattern_why: Selection is the decision itself; the model only collects and lays out evidence for the recruiter.

in_practice.trigger: Final interview stage closes in Recruitee.
steps: Chase missing scorecards with an automatic reminder.
Model builds a comparison from structured scorecards, not from interview summaries alone.
Recruiter writes the recommendation and reasons.
Hiring manager decides and the decision is logged.
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter writes and owns the recommendation; the hiring manager decides.
data_needed: 90-day retention by site and role from AFAS

evidence.claim: AI interview summaries become the record; managers read them instead of the interview and notetakers drop context.
Liability for AI in hiring stays with the employer regardless of vendor contracts.

risks: The comparison replaces the interview in the manager's mind.
A summary records an unlawful question or note about health or pregnancy.
Evaluating candidates becomes high-risk under the AI Act from December 2027.
research_questions: Do hires recommended with the comparison stay past 90 days more often than before?
How many days does automatic scorecard chasing take out of the stage?
Will hiring managers accept structured scorecards over free-text notes?

tasks.short: Tell candidates where their application stands: received, invited, rejected, on hold.

today.trigger: A candidate changes stage in Recruitee or asks for an update.
steps: Check the stage in Recruitee.
Pick a template and adjust it, or call the candidate.
Send rejections after the shortlist is final.
Answer candidates who chase by phone.
drudgery: Sending the same rejection template dozens of times
today.time_sinks: Candidates who wait weeks without news call or email, costing more time than a timely update would.

lenses.faster: Stage-triggered emails with personalised lines go out once the recruiter moves the stage, and a weekly check flags candidates with no news for over ten days; about 65% of the time goes.
lenses.autonomous: A stage change in Recruitee sends the right message; candidates idle past a set number of days get an update automatically; rejections after an interview wait for a recruiter's personal note.
lenses.ambitious: Give every agency-sent flex candidate a status update, a group that never hears back today; demand would grow as agencies ask for the same feed.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copy-pasting rejections; recruiters want more time for the personal call to finalists who just missed out.
lenses.options: None worth having: status messages are fixed by the stage.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns the stage rules and the maximum days a candidate may wait, and watches days per stage instead of sending mail; slightly more expert.
reach: Take over offer and contract status messages from the HR Administrator by learning the AFAS contract workflow.

tasks.human_edge: Calling finalists who were rejected after interviews and handling upset or vulnerable candidates.
tasks.pattern_why: Stage changes and time limits are rules that can be written down and run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Stage change in Recruitee or candidate idle past the set number of days.
steps: Rule selects the template for the stage and language.
Message is sent and logged on the candidate.
Weekly list of idle candidates goes to the recruiter.
Post-interview rejections wait for a recruiter note before sending.
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter handles exceptions and adds a personal note to post-interview rejections.
data_needed: Stage list and templates per language

evidence.claim: Uniper's hiring agent flagged overdue tasks such as candidates on a shortlist for over 14 days; time to contract signature fell 27 days.
Recruitee supports automated emails triggered by pipeline stage changes.

risks: A wrong stage move sends a rejection by mistake.
Cold automatic rejections hurt the employer brand in a tight labour market.
research_questions: What is the median number of days candidates wait without contact per stage today?
Do automatic idle updates reduce inbound 'any news' calls?
How many wrong-stage mails occur in the first month?

tasks.short: Find candidates through job boards, LinkedIn, referrals, agencies and job fairs when applications fall short.

today.trigger: A vacancy has too few suitable applicants or a hard-to-fill role opens (truck drivers, maintenance technicians).
steps: Search LinkedIn, job boards and the Recruitee talent pool.
Write and send outreach messages.
Ask employees for referrals and agencies for profiles.
Plan job fairs and regional ads around the three sites.
drudgery: Searching the talent pool by hand for past silver medallists
today.time_sinks: Manual searches and outreach for driver and technician roles with low reply rates.

lenses.faster: An agent searches the Recruitee talent pool and past applicants, drafts outreach per person, and the recruiter approves each send, saving about 35%.
lenses.autonomous: A vacancy below its applicant target after ten days triggers a talent-pool search and draft outreach; the recruiter approves each message before it goes.
lenses.ambitious: Rediscover former flex workers who performed well, a group nobody contacts today, and offer them fixed roles; demand would grow because it is the cheapest source of proven people.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rewriting outreach; recruiters want more time at job fairs and with driver networks.
lenses.options: Testing two or three outreach angles (pay, shift stability, location) per role changes which channel gets the budget.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter decides channel spend per role and site based on source-of-hire and 90-day retention; more expert.
reach: Take over agency spend comparisons from the FP&A Analyst by learning the agency invoice data.

tasks.human_edge: Building trust in driver and technician networks, judging fit from a short conversation, and deciding who is worth pursuing.
tasks.pattern_why: Search paths vary per role and source, so steps cannot be fixed; every outreach needs recruiter approval.

in_practice.trigger: Vacancy below applicant target after a set number of days.
steps: Agent searches the Recruitee talent pool, past applicants and former flex workers.
Agent drafts personalised outreach.
Recruiter approves or edits each message.
Replies flow into the Recruitee pipeline.
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter approves every outreach before it is sent.

evidence.claim: Workday Talent Acquisition Agent flags roles at risk of missing their fill date and drafts outreach; outreach still requires recruiter approval.
A sourcing agent facing candidates must disclose it is AI and for whom.

risks: Contacting people whose talent-pool consent has expired breaks the AVG.
Generic outreach floods channels and lowers reply rates.
research_questions: How many hires in the last year came from past applicants or former flex workers?
How many talent-pool records have valid consent?
Does approved personal outreach beat ads on reply rate for driver roles?

tasks.short: Check whether our selection criteria and tests are fair, legal and predictive, and propose changes.

today.trigger: Yearly review, a complaint, a new role profile, or a request from the HR Director.
steps: Export Recruitee stage data to Excel.
Compare pass rates by gender and age group where recorded.
Review job ads and criteria for wording that excludes groups.
Write recommendations for the HR Director.
today.time_sinks: Preparing data takes most of the time, leaving little for analysis.

lenses.faster: A fixed report gives pass rates per stage and group each quarter and a model flags exclusionary wording in ads and criteria; the recruiter interprets, saving about 35%.
lenses.autonomous: A quarterly run produces the report; the recruiter reviews and decides what to change.
lenses.ambitious: Check whether criteria predict 90-day retention, a decision made far more often (quarterly per role instead of rarely), offered to the HR Director; demand grows once the link is visible.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses cleaning exports; recruiters want more time on why a criterion fails a group.
lenses.options: Comparing pass rates under alternative criteria (e.g. certificate required versus trainable) changes the rule chosen.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter becomes the reviewer of selection criteria with evidence from retention, and the competent overseer the AI Act will require; more expert.
reach: Take over hiring-funnel reporting from the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst by learning Power BI data modelling.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a difference is unfair or job-related, and defending criteria to the works council and in a complaint.
tasks.pattern_why: The analysis is a judgment on fairness and law; software feeds the numbers and the recruiter decides.

in_practice.trigger: Quarterly schedule or a new role profile.
steps: Scheduled report computes stage pass rates and retention per criterion.
Model flags ad and criteria wording that may exclude groups.
Recruiter reviews and drafts revisions.
HR Director approves changes.
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter interprets results; HR Director approves revisions.

evidence.claim: Disparate impact claims continue against hiring tools; the employer stays liable.
From 2 December 2027 filtering and evaluating candidates is high-risk, needing a competent overseer and logs kept six months.
The AP finds recruitment AI weak on explainability.

risks: Small numbers per site make pass-rate differences noise.
Collecting group data for monitoring needs an AVG basis.
research_questions: Is there enough recorded gender and age data to compute meaningful pass rates per site?
Which current criteria show any link to 90-day retention?
What will the AI Act overseer role require from this recruiter in December 2027?

tasks.short: Plan how we will fill seasonal peaks and hard roles across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

today.trigger: Annual planning, the run-up to the Q4 peak, or a new customer contract at a site.
steps: Collect headcount plans from site managers.
Review time to hire, source of hire and agency use in Power BI and Excel.
Agree the mix of fixed hires and agency flex workers.
Present the plan to the HR Director and site managers.
drudgery: Merging agency hours and invoices with AFAS headcount
Building the same slides each year
today.time_sinks: Data gathering from three agencies and three sites.

lenses.faster: A model summarises days per stage, stuck candidates, agency fill rates and cost per site into a draft plan; the recruiter sets the strategy, saving about 30%.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly run compares open roles with fill-date risk and flags where the plan is slipping; strategy changes stay with the recruiter.
lenses.ambitious: Revisit the fixed-versus-flex mix per site monthly instead of yearly, for the Finance Director and site managers; demand would grow as agency costs become visible.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses merging agency spreadsheets; recruiters want more time with site managers on the plan.
lenses.options: Scenarios (more fixed hires before Q4 versus more agency use) change the decision and its cost.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns the hiring plan per site with budget input, gaining a say over agency spend; more expert.
reach: Take over agency cost forecasting from the FP&A Analyst by learning the cost model.

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with site managers and agencies, and reading the local labour market around each site.
tasks.pattern_why: Strategy is a judgment with stakeholders; the model prepares the evidence and scenarios.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly planning cycle or a new customer contract.
steps: Pull days per stage, fill-date risk and agency fill rates.
Model drafts scenarios with cost and risk.
Recruiter chooses and presents the plan.
HR Director and site managers agree.
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter and HR Director decide the strategy.

evidence.claim: With process context, Uniper's agent found specific bottlenecks such as 27 candidates shortlisted for over 14 days; on raw data it gave generalities.
Under 5% of companies saw transformational results from AI in hiring.

risks: Agency data in different formats gives wrong comparisons.
Plans look precise but ignore local labour market shifts.
research_questions: Can agency hours and invoices be joined to AFAS headcount per site each month?
Which roles miss their fill date most often and why?
Does a monthly scenario review change agency spend?

tasks.short: Set up and run applicant tests such as forklift practicals, language checks and reach truck tests.

today.trigger: A vacancy requires a test, or a site asks for a new test.
steps: Pick or write the test with the site trainer.
Schedule test slots at the site.
Collect results from the trainer.
Review whether the test predicts performance.
today.time_sinks: Coordinating trainers and candidates across three sites.

lenses.faster: A model drafts written test items and scoring guides from the role profile and a booking tool handles slots; the recruiter and trainer review, saving about 25%.
lenses.autonomous: Booking and result entry run automatically; test content and pass marks stay with the recruiter and trainer.
lenses.ambitious: Offer a short language and safety test to agency flex workers before their first shift, a group not tested today; demand would grow as sites see fewer incidents.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses typing results; recruiters want more time on making tests fair and job-related.
lenses.options: Two versions of a test checked against later performance change which one is used.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns test validity with the trainers; more expert.
reach: Take over test design work from the Learning and Development Specialist by learning Studytube course building.

tasks.human_edge: Observing practical skill and safety behaviour, and judging whether a test is fair for non-native speakers.
tasks.pattern_why: Test design and pass marks are judgments; the model drafts and the person leads.

in_practice.trigger: New role profile or a test review.
steps: Model drafts test items and scoring guide.
Recruiter and trainer review and approve.
Booking tool schedules candidates.
Results go to Recruitee.
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter and trainer approve tests and pass marks.

evidence.claim: Workday's TA team generated interview questions for 800+ skills across 1,600+ roles, with no evidence of better hires.
Emotion inference in hiring is banned under AI Act Art. 5(1)(f).

risks: Generated items test reading ability, not the job.
Language tests disadvantage non-native speakers unfairly.
research_questions: Do current test scores predict 90-day retention or incidents?
Would a pre-shift test for flex workers reduce first-week incidents?
Can Studytube host applicant tests separate from employee courses?

role.altitude: From reading CVs and sending emails to running the hiring pipeline by days per stage and 90-day retention, owning the screening criteria, test validity and the human oversight the AI Act will require.
reach: HR Administrator: certificate checks and contract status messages
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: role fact sheets from CAO scales
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: hiring-funnel reporting in Power BI
Learning and Development Specialist: applicant test design in Studytube
role.ceiling_note: Selection, interviews and recommendations stay human by law (GDPR Art. 22, AI Act high-risk from December 2027) and need OR consent; the gains are in status mail, questions and sourcing, roughly 35-40% of role hours.
skills_to_grow: Basic selection statistics and adverse impact
AI Act and AVG oversight duties
Writing approved fact sheets and stage rules
role.ambitious_version: The recruiter runs one pipeline for fixed hires and agency flex workers across three sites, reports monthly which criteria and sources predict 90-day retention, and steers agency spend with Finance.
